headline: Weekend halt continues after a hawkish Jackson Hole Friday: NQ settled at 29,509.50 with equity volatility contained
body: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address on Friday reset September policy expectations, with market-implied odds of a rate increase rising to roughly 60% from about 35% beforehand on CME FedWatch pricing. The repricing was expressed mainly in rates: the 2-year Treasury yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.34%, its highest in a month, the 10-year added roughly 5 basis points to 4.72% and the 30-year finished near 5.21%, a policy-led flattening rather than a term-premium shock. Equity damage stayed contained and internally split. Cash NDX closed at 29,433.43 (-0.70%) within a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range and NQ September futures settled the week at 29,509.50 (-0.63%) in a 29,436.75-29,811.50 range, both in the lower part of their session ranges, but the decline was rotational: semiconductors gave back part of the Nvidia-led advance while several other large index members finished higher and the Dow ended roughly unchanged. VIX closed at 14.43 in a 14.13-14.84 range, so implied volatility did not confirm a stress event. Energy stayed a stabilising input, with WTI settling at $83.40 after a weekly decline of about 4% and Brent at $89.31, down more than 5% on the week, as Hormuz corridor mediation continued without a finalised agreement. Since the 21:00Z settlement no Nasdaq-100 venue has been open, so the current assessment adds no new price-path evidence to Friday's verified close. Tail is held at 6 because the pathological no-retracement path it measures requires a live market, and Stress at 24 reflects the deferred gap and weekend headline risk carried into the Sunday 22:00Z reopen. The shared Finviz cross-asset file was collected at 19:37Z Friday and is outside the freshness window, so it was treated as stale context only; its latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor readings are consistent with the rotational close described above but were not used as price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours span Friday's full trading day and the start of the weekend halt. Overnight Asian and European hours held Tail near 11-12 with Stress around 49-55 and a mixed mode. Tail and Stress lifted through the U.S. morning as the Jackson Hole address reset September rate expectations, peaking at Tail 22 and Stress 64 in the 17:00Z hour with an event/whipsaw mode while short yields rose. Price discovery stayed orderly: retracements occurred, VIX eased rather than spiked and the decline was rotational rather than broad, so Tail never approached the block threshold. After the 20:00Z cash close and the 21:00Z futures settlement, Tail and Stress fell to weekend levels of 6-8 and 25-30 with a normal mode. One slot, the 10:00Z hour, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The published window runs from the current hour through Saturday 23:00Z and contains no cash session, no CME futures session and no scheduled U.S. release; the Sunday 22:00Z reopen sits 23 hours beyond the final slot. With no venue open, the pathological no-retracement path that Tail measures cannot form, so Tail is held at a 6-7 floor throughout and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with no danger window. Stress decays from 24 to a weekend trough of 19 through the European Saturday hours before rebuilding to 24 by the end of the window as the interval of unpriced weekend information widens ahead of the reopen. Confidence declines gradually from 83 to 76, which is an ageing adjustment rather than a sign of conflicting sources: Friday's closing data, yields, oil and volatility are verified and internally consistent, but the newest market observation keeps growing older with no tick able to replace it. The genuine risk carried across this window is a single reopen gap plus weekend headline flow, principally the unresolved Strait of Hormuz mediation and any further policy commentary on the closing day of the symposium. A gap alone is not the repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures, so gap risk is carried in Stress and Confidence until live structure can be observed after the reopen.
